statement.p: A particle moves on a circle of radius 6 cm, centered at the origin, in the xy-plane (x and y measured in centimeters). At time t=0 it starts at the point (0,6) and moves counterclockwise as t increases, going once around the circle in 8 seconds at constant speed.
(a) Write a parameterization for the particle's motion.

static.solution:
(a) For any positive constant k, the parameterization x=-6\sin(kt)\quad y=6\cos(kt) moves counterclockwise on a circle of radius 6 starting at the point (0,6). We choose k to make the period 8 seconds. If k\cdot 8=2\pi, then k=\pi/4 and the parameterization is x=-6\sin\left(\frac {\pi t}{4}\right)\qquad y=6\cos \left(\frac {\pi t}{4}\right).
(b) Since it takes 8 seconds for the particle to go around the circle \mbox{Speed}=\frac{\mbox{Circumference of circle}}{8} = \frac {2\pi(6)}{8} = \frac {3\pi}{2}\mbox{ cm/sec}.
